passages.provision_quote: This bill would authorize a local jurisdiction, if specified conditions are met, to allow for the preparation or sale of noncannabis food or beverage products, as specified, by a licensed retailer or microbusiness in the area where the consumption of cannabis is allowed, and to allow, and to sell tickets for, live musical or other performances on the premises of a licensed retailer or microbusiness in the area where the consumption of cannabis is allowed.
passages.note: Authorizes ancillary food/beverage and music at already-licensed cannabis lounges; does not speak to the legal-status question the rungs differ on.
Final concurrence vote on the same ancillary-amenities bill; the tally shows he voted Aye but not on any clause the rungs separate.
passages.actor_quote: Garcia, Gipson, Grayson, Haney, Hart, Holden

rows.reasoning: AB 1775 only lets a local jurisdiction permit noncannabis food, beverage, and live-music sales at already-licensed cannabis consumption lounges; it leaves the legal-status and commercial-licensing questions the rungs differ on (criminal penalties vs. medical-only vs. decriminalized possession vs. licensed taxed market vs. minimal restriction) untouched, so both the authorship and the concurrence vote are adjacent and no passage survives to support a chair.
needs_source: Haney's own act or statement directly addressing the cannabis legal-status/commercial-licensing question itself (e.g., sponsorship or vote on the AUMA/MAUCRSA licensing or penalty framework)
